claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix.
The fcc matrix provides formability, strength, and fatigue performance.
Elevated-temperature exposure selectively oxidizes Cr and Ti in this alloy.
Selective Cr and Ti oxidation produces a thin, protective, adherent oxide scale.
Cr and Ti segregate toward the surface at high temperature to form the protective oxide layer.
An intact oxide scale passivates the substrate and limits further oxidation.
Higher oxygen partial pressure or prolonged exposure can cause scale thickening or spallation.
Scale thickening or spallation permits deeper oxygen ingress.
Deeper oxygen ingress initiates internal oxidation.
Internal oxidation undermines the alloy's mechanical integrity.
Samples retaining a thin, adherent scale and showing limited 18O penetration will undergo minimal loss of strength and fatigue life relative to baseline.
Samples exhibiting scale deterioration, substantial 18O subsurface penetration, and internal oxidation will undergo accelerated mechanical degradation.
Under standard-air exposure at the testing temperature, oxide-scale formation is naturally self-limiting and protective.
The proposed oxidation mechanism applies over 800–1000 °C under controlled laboratory oxygen partial pressures.
Outside the stated temperature and oxygen-pressure boundaries, alternative degradation modes may operate.
Differences in scale thickness, adherence, and 18O penetration should track differences in degradation across oxygen partial pressures and reducing controls.
